title: Make your own tree
summary: Create a tree, give it a root node, and save it.

say.never: A **tree** is one autonomous routine, saved in a file. You'll make a new one called `MyFirstAuto`, give it a **root node** (the one node at the very top, that everything else hangs under), and save it.
say.bit: Make a tree called `MyFirstAuto`, give it a root node, save.

say.never: Click **+ New tree**, at the top of the **Trees** list on the left.
Type `MyFirstAuto` in the **Tree ID** box. Leave **A new file** picked, so it gets a file of its own. Then click **Create**.

waitFor.hint: name it MyFirstAuto and click Create.

say.never: A tree has exactly **one** node at the top: its **root node**. Every other step hangs underneath it. To run several steps in a row, the root is a **Sequence**, the node that runs its children in order. Your new tree is empty, so the canvas offers to add one.
say.bit: Every tree has one **root node** at the top. Yours will be a **Sequence**.

say.never: In the middle of the empty canvas, click **Add root node**. A list of nodes pops up.

Type `Sequence` and pick the one called just **Sequence** (not AsyncSequence or ReactiveSequence). It becomes your tree's root node. (Dragging **Sequence** from the Nodes list onto the canvas does the same.)

waitFor.hint: pick Sequence as the root node.

say.never: Press **Save** at the top (or **Ctrl+S**). The little dot next to the file name disappears once it's saved. Until you save, nothing is written to the file the robot runs, and a new tree that was never saved is gone if the page reloads.
say.bit: **Save** (Ctrl+S). The dot by the file name goes away.
